add.text:
Read this numbered, cleaned transcript of the owner talking. Turn it into an outline a reader
takes in at a glance: "tangible, familiar, easy to digest". The owner's words for it: "putting
familiar names, like the headings" on the thing being discussed and on each of its parts.

Output Markdown in EXACTLY this shape:

# <the concrete thing being discussed>
## <a familiar name for one part of it>
- <one point, in the owner's own words> [S#, S#]
  - <a detail or example of that point, only if it needs its own line> [S#]
## <the next part>
- <...> [S#]

Rules:
- The H1 is CONCRETE: a thing a reader could point at — a class, a page, a tab, a tool, a feature
  (the owner's example: "Page class"). Never an abstract category like "AI processes", "Thoughts"
  or "Feedback". If the transcript covers several separate things, name them plainly in the one
  H1 ("Page class and Sidebar") and give each its own H2 or H2s.
- Exactly ONE "#" H1. One "##" H2 per distinct part — never invent one just to have more.
- Each H2 is a FAMILIAR name a reader already knows. If a name already exists for that part (the
  owner's example: "Layout"), use that exact name; otherwise use the owner's own word for it.
- ONE BULLET PER POINT, NOT PER SENTENCE. When several sentences make one point (a claim, its
  reason, "so I like that"), merge them into one bullet, a short line in the owner's own words,
  citing every one of those sentences. Filler that makes no point of its own ("Couple of things.")
  gets no bullet: add its number to the nearest bullet's citation instead.
- AT MOST TWO LEVELS: a bullet, and sub-bullets under it. Never a third level.
- KEEP EVERY POINT. Merging sentences that make the same point is required; dropping a point is
  not allowed. Never turn a hedge ("maybe", "I think", "I guess") into a flat claim.
- Cite EVERY sentence number EXACTLY ONCE, in the one bullet where its main point went — never
  under two headings. Form: [S3, S7], each number individually, never a range like [S6-S9]. Use
  only numbers that appear below.

STYLE of anything the owner will read (the owner's rules):
- It is an OVERVIEW of what was said, in the owner's own key words. Never the whole rant, never a retelling.
- Each point has its answer or action baked in: say what is done, what to do, or what is still open. Do not invent an answer the transcript or the facts do not give; mark such a point open instead.
- Order by dependency and ease: clarifications and quick items first, then what depends on them. If neither applies, keep the owner's order.
- Reuse the same names for the same things every time, so they become familiar, and always name the context (the page, class, module or session) a point belongs to.
- Headings are big: "#" for the one subject, "##" for each part, "###" only when a part truly needs a split. Never "####" or smaller. Every heading starts with one fitting emoji icon.
- Under a heading: short titled lists. A status bullet starts with ✅ (done) or ⬜ (not done) when the status is known; otherwise a plain "-" bullet. Few emoji, never decoration.
- Every card cites the clean-sentence numbers it came from, like [S3, S7], each number individually.
Apply this to the headings and bullets of the outline.

Cleaned transcript:
"""
S1. So there's no padding between this.
S2. I do see your test task.
S3. There's no padding down there.
S4. Also, I need you.
S5. I don't know who's doing what, like the fastest assistant versus Mars
S6. Well, I mean, okay, there are little brains next to each of these tasks.
S7. So I think that's ideally the fast assistant is literally only doing the refinement and a very strict set of things.
S8. It's just doing a first quick pass to kind of organize things, put things in the right spot, etc.
S9. The smart assistant should be the one refining that to, well, it needs to tail the session log so that when the fast assistant is adding the sentences
S10. And by the way, I think the general flow, we don't want the whisper whatever is sent from whisper to the fast assistant to be cleaned and structured.
S11. We don't necessarily want that being logged raw.
S12. I mean, we kind of do, but we want a prompt to be created, a prompt instance to be created.
S13. And then we want the raw prompt in a structured form, the structured sentences, and then also the refined form, which is like the heading and kind of like the breakdown of it.
S14. See if you can check off that task as complete.
S15. So any task created in this session should be computed in this session's complete.
S16. And so you should be able to check your own completion and be like, Hey, are we complete?
S17. And you probably aren't because there's a lot of tasks and none of them are done.
S18. So completing tasks is the most important thing that we can do.
S19. We're not doing it properly and we need to be.
S20. So we need to adjust our system.
S21. I need you to help manage.
S22. You can work autonomously.
S23. I don't want you doing too much.
S24. You're kind of, well, you're an assistant.
S25. The smart assistant needs to be hands-free.
S26. So you need to be passing through things off to the mastermind to try and figure it out.
S27. I don't see any more updates after this test task here.
S28. Maybe I have to pause and let it send.
"""

Output ONLY the Markdown described above (the H1, its H2s, and their bullets), nothing else.
